name: WES NA12878 somatic variant benchmark
description: Bioinformatic analysis of genomic sequencing data to identify somatic mutations in cancer samples is far from achieving the required robustness and standardisation. In this study we generated a whole exome sequencing benchmark dataset using the platinum genome sample NA12878 and developed an intersect-then-combine (ITC) approach to increase the accuracy in calling single nucleotide variants (SNVs) and indels in tumour-normal pairs. We evaluated the effect of alignment, base quality recalibration, mutation caller and filtering on sensitivity and false positive rate. The ITC approach increased the sensitivity up to 17.1%, without increasing the false positive rate per megabase (FPR/Mb) and its validity was confirmed in a set of clinical samples.
evaluation_method: sensitivity and false_positive_rate_per_mb (FPR/Mb); also precision/recall and F1 reported
notes: Non-LLM bioinformatics benchmark using whole-exome data from NA12878; results depend heavily on aligner, recalibration, caller and filters. Limited to WES (not whole genome), can be saturated for SNVs, and indel performance is generally lower.
